evals.name: most-vague-asks-for-material
evals.expected_output: One batch reply: a short statement of what it understood, a tagged draft brief, and questions with recommendations and concrete options. No prompt yet.
expectations: The reply contains no image-generation prompt
The reply states in plain words what it understood the ask to be
It asks what material the user already has (a screenshot, a number, a before/after, an output)
It offers two or three concrete subject directions rather than an open 'what should it show?'
Brief lines are tagged [user], [doc] or [proposed]
It asks where the user will generate the image
All questions arrive in a single reply, not one at a time

evals.name: placed-ask-infers-production
evals.prompt: a hero image for the docs site
evals.expected_output: Infers a production asset with live text over it; proposes the brief and asks only the open, work-changing questions.
expectations: Mode is proposed as a production asset
In-image text is proposed as none, with space reserved for live HTML text
Destiny (whole-frame vs cutout vs text overlay) is raised as a question or confirmed explicitly
It asks which tool or model the user will generate with
No prompt is written before the user answers
It does not invent a house style; style comes from documented rules or a question with options

evals.name: fast-lane-midjourney-encoding
evals.prompt: Write a Midjourney prompt for a 16:9 background for our pricing section. Text sits on the left third. Dark navy with one amber accent, no people, not a cutout. Everything's decided, just write it.
evals.expected_output: Shows the brief and writes the prompt in the same reply, encoded for Midjourney.
expectations: The prompt is written in the same reply (fast lane), with the brief shown
The prompt ends with a parameter string including --ar 16:9
Exclusions use --no with bare nouns; the prompt text contains no 'no people' or 'without' phrasing
The left third is described as empty or quiet space for text
No in-image text is requested
The anchor block or deliverable names Midjourney as the family it was tuned on

evals.name: nano-banana-positive-restatement
evals.prompt: I'll use Gemini. Product shot of our plain white mug on a wooden desk, morning light, no logos, no text, no people. 4:5. Go ahead.
evals.expected_output: A Nano Banana prompt in full sentences with exclusions restated positively and the ratio at the end.
expectations: The prompt is written in full sentences, not comma-separated keywords
Exclusions are phrased as positive states (e.g. 'a plain unbranded white mug', 'an empty room') rather than 'no logos' / 'no text' / 'no people'
The ratio (4:5) appears in the prompt text, near the end
Light direction is stated, not just 'morning light'
Camera height, angle and framing are stated

evals.name: real-person-likeness-and-reference-role
evals.prompt: I've got a selfie of my cofounder. Make a LinkedIn cover of her presenting on stage at our launch.
evals.expected_output: Asks how the cofounder's likeness may be used and treats the selfie as an identity-only reference with the camera stated explicitly.
expectations: It asks how the cofounder's likeness may be used before writing a prompt
It states the selfie will carry identity only
It plans to state camera height, angle, distance and framing explicitly rather than inherit them from the selfie
It does not propose depicting the cofounder saying or endorsing something specific without confirmation

evals.name: unowned-reference-described-not-uploaded
evals.prompt: Use this photo I found on Pinterest as the style reference for our cover: https://example.com/found-photo.jpg
evals.expected_output: Declines to pass the found image to a model as a reference; offers to describe its light, composition and palette in words instead.
expectations: It does not include the found image as an attached or URL reference in any prompt or settings
It explains that an image the user doesn't own is described in words rather than uploaded
It offers to translate the liked properties (light, composition, palette) into prompt text

evals.name: iterate-one-change-preserve-list
evals.prompt: Here's what ChatGPT gave me for the launch cover: the timer reads 25:00 instead of 20:00, and there's a Nike swoosh on the mug in the corner. Everything else is great. Fix it.
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses both misses, fixes one per pass with a full preserve list, and removes the brand mark by positive restatement.
expectations: It does not regenerate from scratch; it writes an edit instruction
The edit changes only one thing per pass (timer first or logo first, not both in one instruction)
The edit restates a full preserve list (composition, camera, lighting, palette, headline, etc.)
The brand mark is removed by positive restatement ('a plain unbranded white mug') without naming Nike or the swoosh in the edit
It explains how to apply the edit in ChatGPT (same conversation, image attached or area selected)

evals.name: unlisted-model-safe-defaults
evals.prompt: I generate with a model on Krea that isn't any of the big ones. Write the prompt for a dark moody product hero of our headphones, 16:9. Go.
evals.expected_output: Uses the safe defaults for an uncharacterized model and flags the first pass as calibration.
expectations: It says the model is not characterized and the first pass is a calibration pass
The prompt uses full sentences with the focal subject first
Exclusions are phrased as positive states
Lighting is given as a measurement (exposure reference, share of frame in shadow), not only mood words
The ratio appears in the prompt and is also listed as a setting to set where the tool has one

evals.name: no-fixed-camera-default
evals.prompt: Portrait of our CTO for the team page. Use the attached headshot for likeness, she's fine with it. ChatGPT. No particular style.
evals.expected_output: Does not default to eye-level straight-on 85mm; proposes contrasting framings and, with no look to follow, suggests mw-image-direction when it is installed.
expectations: The camera line is not silently set to eye level, straight on, ~85mm
It proposes two or three framings that differ in height, distance or placement, and asks the user to pick
With no documented style and no direction chosen, it suggests mw-image-direction (when installed) as a question and does not switch without a yes, or offers concrete style options
If a wide, very low or very high framing is proposed, it notes the likeness trade-off

evals.name: direction-outranks-docs-on-look
evals.prompt: Earlier in this chat we picked a look with mw-image-direction: Cinematic film still, night practicals. Our docs/brand.md says bright high-key product look and 1920x1080 heroes. Write the GPT-Image prompt for the homepage hero of our espresso machine.
evals.expected_output: Uses the chosen direction for the look and takes only the size from the docs.
expectations: Style, lighting and palette follow the cinematic night-practicals direction, tagged [direction]
The 1920x1080 size comes from the docs, tagged [doc]
The docs' high-key look is not used and not blended in
Lighting is written as a measurement (shadow share or exposure reference) rather than mood words alone

evals.name: direction-handoff-not-reasked
evals.prompt:
Confirmed — here's the direction from mw-image-direction:
[direction] Look: Analog film, warm consumer color
[direction] Images: one homepage hero, 1600x900
[direction] Destiny: whole frame, live HTML headline over it
[direction] Text zone: right 40%, plaster wall in shadow, one value
[direction] Generator: Nano Banana (Gemini)
[direction] Shot A: candid over the counter; loaf lower-left on a dark walnut board, baker's hands dusting flour over it, face turned away and cropped; one low morning sun from camera-left, long shadows to the right; the floured ridge brightest and sharpest
[direction] Style block: (pasted verbatim)
Write the prompt.
evals.expected_output: Treats every [direction] line as settled, shows the brief with those tags, asks nothing about destiny, generator, image list or text zone, and writes the Nano Banana prompt in the same reply.
expectations: It does not ask about destiny, the generator, the image list or the text zone
The brief carries those lines tagged [direction]
The prompt is written in the same reply, or after at most one question about something no [direction] line settles
The prompt is encoded for Nano Banana: full sentences, exclusions phrased as positive states
The right 40% is described as a quiet plaster wall in shadow for the headline, with no in-image text
The staging lines appear as visible results (placement, contact, light side and shadow direction, brightest and sharpest point) within the family's budget (at most 8 physics clauses)
The style block is used word for word, not paraphrased

evals.name: midjourney-respects-staging-budget
evals.prompt: Direction is confirmed, generator is Midjourney. The scene sheet for the hero: round sourdough loaf 22 cm, about a fifth of the frame width, lower-left third; dark oiled walnut board on an oak counter; contact shadow under the loaf; one low morning sun from camera-left about 15° up, shadows to the right about 3.7× the height; the floured scored ridge is brightest and sharpest; baker's face turned away and cropped at the brow; f/2.8, the face only a touch soft; plaster wall 2.4 m back, about 4 stops darker; proving baskets soft on a shelf; flour only on the crust ridge; scraper mid-stroke. 16:9, headline over the right 40%. Write the prompt.
evals.expected_output: A Midjourney prompt whose staging stays within 4 physics clauses and about 50 words, chosen in the prompt-budget order, with the rest left on the sheet; a parameter line beside it.
expectations: The prompt contains at most 4 physics clauses (placement, contact, light and shadows, emphasis), and the staging text is about 50 words or fewer
The clauses follow the priority order: hero with share and placement, then what it rests on and its contact, then light side and shadow direction, then brightest and sharpest
The prompt contains no centimetres, metres, f-numbers, stops or degrees
It says the remaining sheet lines are kept for checking the render, not added to the prompt
The prompt ends with a parameter string that includes --ar 16:9, and exclusions use --no with bare nouns
The right 40% is described as quiet space for the headline, with no in-image text

evals.name: fake-render-one-float-one-edit
evals.prompt: Here's the Gemini render of our ceramic mug on the desk (attached) with the prompt I used. Everything is right — placement, light, colours — except the mug floats a little above the desk. Fix it.
evals.expected_output: One edit that adds the missing contact, with a full preserve list; no regeneration.
expectations: It writes one edit instruction, not a new prompt from scratch
The edit adds contact in visible terms: the mug's base resting flat on the desk with a soft contact shadow where it touches, on the side away from the light
The edit changes only that one thing
The edit restates a full preserve list (composition, camera, lighting, palette, the mug itself)
It explains how to apply the edit in Gemini (same conversation, image attached)

evals.name: fake-render-scale-camera-regenerate
evals.prompt: This Midjourney render looks fake (attached, with my prompt). The coffee cup is as big as the laptop beside it, the camera looks straight down although I wanted the desk seen from a low angle, and the shadows go two ways.
evals.expected_output: Classifies it as a scale and camera failure and regenerates from re-derived staging instead of chaining edits.
expectations: It does not write a chain of edit passes; it regenerates
It names the wrong scale, the wrong camera and the disagreeing shadows as the problems

It re-derives the staging before rewriting the prompt (or routes to mw-image-direction's render diagnosis when it is installed): the cup's size relative to the laptop, the camera height and angle, and one light with shadows falling one way
The new prompt states the scale relation as a visible result (for example the cup about a third of the laptop's width) rather than in centimetres
The new prompt keeps the Midjourney staging budget (at most 4 physics clauses)

evals.name: variation-on-staged-image
evals.prompt: Here's the Midjourney prompt we just wrote for the bakery hero (16:9, headline over the right 40%), staged with mw-image-direction: "a round sourdough loaf on a dark walnut board in the lower left, a baker's hands dusting flour over it, face turned away and cropped at the brow; low morning sun from the left casting long shadows to the right; the floured scored ridge is the brightest, sharpest point" plus the style block and parameters. Give me one or two variations as a fallback, and make one of them from a higher angle.
evals.expected_output: Variations change placement or the instant within the same staging; the higher-angle variation re-derives its staging lines. Style, light logic and palette stay fixed.
expectations: Each variation is labelled as a variation
Style block, palette and light logic are unchanged across the variations
A variation that keeps the camera changes only placement or the instant (for example the scraper mid-stroke vs. lifting away)
The higher-angle variation re-derives its staging lines: the loaf's frame share and placement, where the light falls in frame, the shadow direction and the quiet zone for the headline
No variation that moves the camera copies the original staging clauses unchanged
Each variation keeps the Midjourney staging budget (at most 4 physics clauses)

evals.name: seamless-tile-midjourney-v8
evals.prompt: A seamless repeating terrazzo texture for our website background. I'll use Midjourney. Write it.
evals.expected_output: A Midjourney tile prompt using --tile on V8.2, with no focal subject.
expectations: The parameter string includes --tile
The version is V8.2 (or the current V8), and --tile is not pinned to V7
It does not use --q
If it mentions editing, it notes --tile does not work with the Edit model
The prompt describes an even, all-over pattern with no focal subject, border or vignette
